name: Palestinian nationalism
summary: Palestinian nationalism is the national movement of the Palestinian Arabs for self-determination and sovereignty in Palestine. It holds that Palestinians are one people with an inherent identity and a right of return, that the loss of 1948 and the occupation of 1967 are illegitimate, and that they are owed a state with Jerusalem as capital. The mainstream, the PLO and Fatah, moved from armed struggle for all of Mandatory Palestine to a state on the 1967 territories alongside Israel; its Islamist wing, Hamas, keeps armed resistance and rejects recognition.
scope: The national question only: the Palestinian people, its territory, return, sovereignty, Jerusalem, relations with Zionism and the Arab nation, and the means accepted. Taken from the PLO's Covenant of 1968, the 1974 programme, Arafat's 1974 UN speech, Fatah's constitution, the 1988 Declaration of Independence and National Council communique, and the 1993 letters of recognition, with Hamas's 2017 Document of General Principles as the Islamist strand where it differs. Where the PLO texts differ across time the 1988-1993 position is the committed adherent's present view. The economy, welfare, social policy and the wider programme of Fatah, the PLO or the Palestinian Authority are not counted unless the national texts state them.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The National Council demands withdrawal from all territories occupied in 1967 including Arab Jerusalem, annulment of all measures of annexation and removal of settlements, and invokes the inadmissibility of acquiring territory by force.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The Covenant makes anyone born after 1947 to a Palestinian father a Palestinian wherever born, and Hamas repeats this, but the sources do not set it against birth on the territory.

civilizational-union.rationale: The Declaration says Palestine is one with the Arab nation in heritage and civilization and in its aspiration for unity, and Hamas holds that the unity of the Islamic Ummah must be protected.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Covenant rejects all forms of intervention, trusteeship and subordination, and Arafat looks to a world free of colonialism and imperialism.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Arafat holds up a world free of colonialism and neo-colonialism and calls the Mandate a device to serve the Zionist invaders, and the Covenant voids the Mandate.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The Declaration pairs majority rule with respect for minority rights under a constitution, the rule of law and an independent judiciary, so courts are meant to limit what a majority does.

democracy-best.rationale: The Declaration chooses a parliamentary democratic system based on freedom of expression and party formation, and Hamas accepts democracy as the basis of Palestinian relations, but neither says it holds even when voters choose badly.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The Declaration calls Palestine the state of Palestinians wherever they may be and affirms the right of return for the dispersed, though the texts speak of return and a state for them rather than naturalisation as such.

dominated-front.rationale: The National Council calls for cooperation with socialist, non-aligned, Islamic and African states and all national liberation movements against imperialism, Fatah's constitution makes its struggle part of the world struggle against colonialism and imperialism, and the Declaration commits the state to non-alignment.

elective-rulers.rationale: The Declaration promises a parliamentary democratic system with freedom to form parties, which leaves no place for a ruler who inherits the throne; it does not speak of a head of state.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Declaration promises complete equality of rights and non-discrimination in public rights on grounds of race, religion, colour or sex, and Fatah's constitution seeks equal legal rights without racial or religious discrimination.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Covenant defines Palestinians as Arab nationals, while the Declaration and Arafat promise equal rights to Christians, Jews and Muslims and Hamas's 2017 document counts all Palestinians whatever their religion or culture, so the sources point both ways.

force-without-un.rationale: The Declaration commits the state to the UN Charter, rejects the threat or use of force against other states' territorial integrity and keeps only the right to defend its own.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The Declaration grounds Palestinian rights in natural, historical and legal rights and Hamas treats the land as a consecrated waqf, but the PLO also accepts the partition resolution and a compromise on the 1967 lines, so the sources do not settle the principle (the Covenant's denial of Jewish ties was nullified in 1996).

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The Covenant and the Declaration insist on the return of the dispersed to the homeland, and the National Council rejects resettlement elsewhere, which is the opposite of treating the homeland as only a centre for a diaspora.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The Declaration speaks of an undying union between the people and its land, which it holds through successive generations' sacrifices, and Hamas makes Palestine a consecrated waqf; the Covenant article on the spiritual bond and armed defence was nullified in 1996.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The mainstream recognised Israel's right to exist in 1993 and Arafat in 1988 called resolution 181, with its Jewish and Arab states, the basis of legitimacy, but Fatah's 2009 programme totally rejects recognising Israel as a Jewish state and Hamas rejects recognition of the Zionist entity.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The Declaration bows to the sacred spirits of the fallen and pledges to the souls of the sainted martyrs, and the National Council forms a committee to perpetuate the memory of the martyr Abu Jihad.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Hamas's 1988 Covenant says Zionists and Jews secretly work through Freemasons, Rotary clubs and the Protocols to dominate the world and harm Islam (arts. 22, 28, 32), while Hamas's 2017 document and Arafat say the conflict is with Zionism, not Jews, and the PLO texts make no such claim.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Covenant gives the Palestinian people the right to determine their destiny and exercise self-determination and sovereignty, and the 1988 Declaration proclaims the state in exercise of the people's right to self-determination, political independence and sovereignty.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The mainstream accepted a state on the 1967 territories and recognised Israel in 1993, while Hamas holds that no part of Palestine may be conceded and accepts the 1967 lines only as a consensus formula without recognition.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Declaration promises a parliamentary democratic system with freedom to form parties, and Hamas wants the PLO rebuilt on democratic foundations with participation of all forces.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The National Council says the future relationship of the states of Palestine and Jordan should be confederal by the free choice of both peoples, and the 1974 programme looks to a union of confrontation states.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Declaration promises the Palestinians a state in which to enjoy their collective national and cultural identity, and Arafat denounces the theft of Palestinian cultural heritage and vows to preserve the Arab character of the land.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The National Council calls for security and protection for Palestinians in Lebanon and the Declaration makes the state the state of Palestinians wherever they are, though neither frames it as a state's duty to minorities in neighbours.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Declaration promises complete equality of rights and a parliamentary democratic system free of discrimination on grounds of race, which contradicts limiting the vote and office to one racial or ethnic group.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The Declaration rules out discrimination in public rights on grounds of race, religion or colour and Arafat calls for one state without racial or religious discrimination, which contradicts classifying people by race and separating them.

refugee-return.rationale: The Covenant makes every Palestinian, including those born abroad to a Palestinian father, a member of the people with a right to return, and the Declaration and the 1988 resolutions repeat the right of return as inalienable; Hamas says it is individual and collective.

religious-nation.rationale: The Covenant counts Palestinians as Arab nationals and Jews resident before the Zionist invasion as Palestinians, the Declaration promises equal rights regardless of religion, and Hamas says the Palestinian people includes all Palestinians irrespective of religion.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: The National Council demands removal of the settlements Israel built since 1967, and Arafat stresses that Palestine was inhabited mainly by Muslim and Christian Arabs before the Zionist settlement began.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Arafat asks the world to resist Zionist encouragement of Jewish emigration and to open their own countries to Jews instead (the Covenant's article saying Jews are citizens of their states was nullified in 1996).

separated-powers.rationale: The Declaration promises a parliamentary system under a constitution with an independent judiciary, so the courts sit apart from the elected parliament.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Fatah's constitution calls the Israeli presence a Zionist invasion on a colonial base, Arafat calls the settlement of European Jews a colonial invasion that displaced the Arabs, and Hamas's 2017 document calls the Zionist project colonial; the Covenant's article on this was nullified in 1996.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Declaration of Independence promises a constitution that ensures the rule of law and an independent judiciary, which a ruler above the law would contradict, and Arafat repeated it to the General Assembly in 1988.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The Declaration proclaims the state's commitment to the principles and policies of the Non-Aligned Movement.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Declaration guarantees freedom of expression and the freedom to form parties, and Hamas adopts pluralism and national partnership, which contradicts suppressing opposition and independent organisations.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Declaration says the Palestinian people was never separated from Palestine and forged its national identity through its history, and the Covenant calls the identity genuine, inherent and passed from parents to children whatever the dispersal.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Declaration promises equality and non-discrimination in public rights on grounds of sex under a parliamentary democratic system, which settles women's right to vote and hold office.

missingStatements.text: A people living under foreign military occupation has the right to resist it by armed force.
missingStatements.rationale: The Covenant and Fatah make armed struggle the way to liberation, the 1988 National Council renews the right of peoples to resist occupation, and Arafat calls such confrontation legitimate and just.

missingStatements.text: Settlements built by an occupying power in occupied territory should be removed.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1988 National Council demands annulment of annexation measures and removal of the settlements Israel established since 1967.

missingStatements.text: A state may be proclaimed on part of a people's claimed homeland if it renounces force and accepts the existing neighbouring state.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1988 Declaration proclaims a state on Palestinian territory and rejects force, and the 1993 letters recognise Israel's right to exist in peace, while Hamas and the Covenant reject partition.

notes: Searched the Covenant, the 1974 programme and Arafat speech, Fatah's constitution, the 1988 declaration and communique, the 1993 letters and Hamas's 2017 document theme by theme. Government, economy, society, ecology and technology are almost silent because the national texts are about the national question; the Declaration's equal rights, parliamentary democracy and non-discrimination clauses are the only stated positions there. The 1968 Covenant took positions on Israel's legitimacy that the PLO declared inoperative in 1993; the text of the 1996 amendment was not opened, so which articles remain is not settled here. Hamas and the PLO split on recognition, borders and means. Review (2026-10-30): distinct-gender-roles nulled (equal public rights is a narrower case). PNC texts are treated as the national movement's common ground across its factions; Hamas is the separate strand. Deepen pass (2026-10-30): read the PNC political statements of 1977, 1981, 1983, 1984 and 1987, Fatah's 2009 programme, the 1964 Covenant, the 1988 Hamas Covenant, Arafat's 1988 Geneva speech, the 1996 amendment and Arafat's 1998 list of nullified articles (Covenant arts. 6-10, 15, 19-23 and 30 nullified; parts of 1-5, 11-14, 16-18, 25-27, 29 too), and two scholarly surveys of the PNC resolutions. Themes searched: government, culture, society, means, world, economy; the PNC texts and programmes are about the national question and repeat the same positions session after session, so they added few new answers (the Declaration's rule of law, independent judiciary, parliamentary democracy and freedom of expression). The 1964 Basic Law, the 1965-1974 and 1991-1993 session texts, the PFLP's 2000 programme and the DFLP's 1975 programme were opened or found but are Marxist programmes on class and economy or lack full open text, and no answer rests on them; Fatah's 2009 Internal Charter is organisational. Not found as open full text: the 1964 PLO Basic Law, the 1984-1987 session political programmes beyond the statements, Fatah's 2009 Five Points. Answers resting only on nullified Covenant articles were nulled (patriotic-education) or re-sourced. Review (2026-10-30, after the deepen pass): party-controls-media nulled (freedom of expression does not settle it).
